readerQuestion: How can I start a Home Assistant routine from my phone’s alarm, and what works differently on Android and iPhone?
directAnswer: On Android, enable the Companion Next Alarm sensor, verify its reported app/time, then use a native Time trigger with a negative offset. On iPhone, use a selected stopped-alarm Shortcuts event for an after-dismissal routine; it does not provide pre-alarm synchronization. Rehearse with an in-app message and keep the independent phone alarm.

Section 5 supplies a distinct iPhone message rehearsal. The platform and troubleshooting tables separate timestamp, event, connectivity and repetition failures without operating devices.

claimChecks.claim: Android Next Alarm supplies a UTC timestamp, exposes Local Time and Package attributes, and can be unavailable when there is no next alarm; the equivalent Android-only sensor is not supplied on iOS.
Android returns the earliest next alarm across applications. Filtering the returned app does not give access to every later alarm.

A native Time trigger accepts a timestamp entity and signed offset; negative values run earlier, unknown/unavailable sources have no valid schedule, and a positive offset may fail when the source advances first.
Apple Shortcuts distinguishes Is Stopped from Is Snoozed and allows selecting an existing alarm. A stopped event is not advance publication of tomorrow’s alarm time.
Current Companion App Intents documentation marks the new actions beta, requires iOS 17+ for Perform action, uses server/action/JSON action data, and deprecates legacy Call Service.
persistent_notification.create creates a Home Assistant frontend message; reusing notification_id overwrites the same message. It is not a phone push-delivery test.
Single mode prevents overlapping runs only. It does not enforce once per morning or preserve an interrupted run across a restart.
Traces distinguish a missing trigger from a blocked condition or action failure; running actions manually does not verify the real scheduled trigger.
The UI Toggle helper supplies the on/off state checked before the rehearsal action. That start condition is not a command to stop a separate running script.

incomingLinkOpportunities.readerReason: That section mentions Next Alarm as a separate future automation but gives no timing configuration. This guide provides the concrete Android/iPhone input procedure without replacing the existing brightness ramp.
